rationale: The three authored cases match Give.move, Give.copy and Give.promote. Resolve joins every reference's mode; Take clears only the final initialized unique occurrence; Promote replaces that final occurrence by a shared reference to the identical object. Both effects preserve the surrounding object/variable lists and counter. Copy returns a shared reference without any state change when the final reference is already shared. Reference, not Object, contains the mode. This matches the retained sharing-decision input, including leaving a shared container's field modes alone until a field is copied. The description concerns the distinct-key states introduced by the chapter; it is not a theorem about arbitrary duplicate-key lists. For this removal review, a byte comparison against the previous repair packets confirms that all unit/Lean selection/policy/extra inputs in these Shared packets are unchanged. I reread those inputs rather than treating hash equality as a semantic verdict. The active Shared, Unique, Correspondence and Common.Rooted sources are also byte-identical. Inspection of their import lines shows no dependency on the removed flat heap modules; the new finite-map utility imports Std and is not imported by these layers. The Lake configuration retains these four libraries. Changes to the agent guidance remove the obsolete draft as design authority and clarify reference modes, consistent with these declarations. This supports retaining the correspondence conclusion after removal, independently of the renderer fixture migration. The final packet also captures the isolated renderer Lean fixture; the only final delta consists of that additional tool snapshot and the inventory/freshness-regression changes. None changes the reviewed language declarations or assertions.
